question: Question linked to image nº3 58-year-old liver transplant patient with HCV + cirrhosis. After an uncomplicated postoperative period, the patient is referred to his home. Six weeks after the transplant, he was visited in the outpatient clinic, with a low grade of fever, a worsening of the general condition, a GOT level of 60 IU / L (8-40) and a GPT of 65 IU / L (8-50). with a pattern of marked cholestasis (GGT x 10 and FA x 8) with total bilirubin of 1.7 mg / dL (0.3-1). Likewise, a high number of copies of the HCV was appreciated. It was decided to perform a Doppler ultrasound in which a complete arterial thrombosis was reported. In view of these data, a CT scan and a cholangioresonance were requested, the images of which are presented in the figures. For the clinical, analytical and radiological data, indicate which is the most probable diagnosis of the current problem:

options.opa: Acute rejection mediated by antibodies with associated arterial thrombosis.
options.opd: Extensive ischemic injury of intrahepatic bile ducts.
options.ope: Complete thrombosis of intrahepatic portal branches.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Liver transplant" -> "Postoperative period" -> "Low-grade fever" -> "Worsening general condition" -> "Elevated GOT and GPT levels" -> "Marked cholestasis" -> "High HCV viral load" -> "Doppler ultrasound shows complete arterial thrombosis" -> "Possible acute rejection or early HCV recurrence" -> 70%

CHAIN: "Liver transplant" -> "Postoperative period" -> "Low-grade fever" -> "Worsening general condition" -> "Elevated liver enzymes" -> "Marked cholestasis" -> "High HCV viral load" -> "Doppler ultrasound shows complete arterial thrombosis" -> "Cholangioresonance needed to assess biliary complications" -> "Stenosis of biliary anastomosis possible" -> 65%

CHAIN: "Liver transplant" -> "Postoperative period" -> "Low-grade fever" -> "Worsening general condition" -> "Elevated liver enzymes" -> "Marked cholestasis" -> "High HCV viral load" -> "Doppler ultrasound shows complete arterial thrombosis" -> "Extensive ischemic injury of intrahepatic bile ducts possible" -> 60%

CHAIN: "Liver transplant" -> "Postoperative period" -> "Low-grade fever" -> "Worsening general condition" -> "Elevated liver enzymes" -> "Marked cholestasis" -> "High HCV viral load" -> "Doppler ultrasound shows complete arterial thrombosis" -> "Complete thrombosis of intrahepatic portal branches possible" -> 55%
analysis: The patient presents with worsening liver function tests, cholestasis, and high HCV viral load after liver transplantation. The Doppler ultrasound indicates complete arterial thrombosis, which is a significant complication that can lead to ischemic injury of the liver and bile ducts. Given the clinical presentation and the findings, the most likely diagnosis is extensive ischemic injury of intrahepatic bile ducts due to the arterial thrombosis, leading to cholestasis and liver dysfunction.
